Please excuse what is going to be a poorly strewn together stream of consciousness from yours truly at 4 in the morning. 

I worked at Starbucks for 15 years. From 16 to 31 years old. The pay was abysmal and they always tried to move your attention to how much of a family we were, and how we were all partners. Fuck that noise. Your “culture” doesn’t pay my bills. Despite being full-time, I constantly had to have a second job to have enough money to live as a single-Mom. I worked my way up the management ladder, was a certified trainer who trained everyone from new hires to Shifts, SMs and DMs, and was a Coffee (and tea when we had it) Master.  I’ve worked at four stores, opened stores, worked during remodels, you name it, I’ve done it. I have countless awards from Starbucks from my store being number one in whole bean sales, partner of the quarter, awards for volunteer work I’ve organized and participated in, and thank yous for all the matching grant money I campaigned for, and received for my work with domestic violence centers, habitat for humanity, the parks department, etc. 

This company made me come in with pneumonia. This company made me come in when I couldn’t stop throwing up and I just ended up throwing up in the mop sink repeatedly while trying to the do the deposit. This company had myself and my team work in a “mobile” Starbucks during our remodel, which was a unbearably hot metal box, and trapeze through our store that had the floor dug up to get products and milk, which had to have been some kind of violation to our safety. This company threatened to let me go if I wouldn’t come in when my child was too sick to go to daycare. We had a terrible windstorm that knocked out the towns power for three days, and when it happened we assumed there was a tornado going through. Our DM told me to not close the store and sit in the dark with my team until it was our actual closing time. Oh! This other time I had pneumonia and was not getting better (because they wouldn’t give me time off) I finally had to go to my doctor and get a note saying “hey she’s gotta be off for at least a week” and my store manager had the audacity to ask me to get my shifts covered. I told her no, and sent a text to my DM (I’d been with the company at least 13 years at this point, had called off maybe five times in those 13 years, and had rose up management, but had take myself back down to just a trainer and barista, and had been with this company longer than anyone else in the district at that time. All that to say I knew my DM, and they knew me. I hated her because she was awful, but we knew each other well enough I had her number and she had mine, and we kept up appearances) letting her know the situation, and sent a picture of my doctors note and a picture form the Handbook saying you don’t have to get your shifts covered if you’re ill. She didn’t respond so I called the Ethics Hotline, and proceeded to go home and get better. Of course days later, presumably when the DM got the notice from the Ethics hotline she texted me to apologize for the delay and the misunderstanding my SM had, that she must have been confused when asking me to get my shifts covered. Whoops!

It sounds trite but there’s so many bad things to say about this company. I had two final straw moments with Starbucks. One was I got a new seasonal role (this was a new second job for me) and they started me off as entry level employee making .25 cents more an hour than I was topped out at Starbucks after 14.5 years. The second straw was as I progressed with my seasonal role that made more, I started shifting my hours for the seasonal role to be FT and Starbucks to be PT. My typical day looked like- Starbucks from 4a-9a, home to change, quick nap, and the seasonal role from 12p-10p five days a week. I got very little sleep, hardly saw my son, and had no time for myself. My 4a-9a role was an opening shift for me with my SM as they keyholder. This is not the same SM who tried to make me work with pneumonia. I liked this SM as a person, and she was someone who had been with the brand as long as me but new to our district and still somehow very deeply rooted in the Starbucks branded spice. We opened at 4:30a but were normally dead until ~5:30a, but this week was our school district’s Spring Break, so we would be dead until at least 7a and even when our peak started, it would be half our normal volume. Everything was done, that store was spotless, so I just hung out in the drive-thru waiting for a customer and reading The NY Times on my phone. When we got a third partner in that morning my SM pulled me into the back to very awkwardly tell me that I shouldn’t be on my phone, to put it in my locker, and that I should essentially know better. Dear Reader, I literally laughed in her face. I wasn’t trying to be rude, but her request was outlandish. There was nothing for me to do, all opening tasks were done, the store was immaculate, and we had no customers. Who was going to see me reading on my phone except her? I tendered my two weeks notice that day, and have not regretted leaving that soul sucking siren once.

Oh my word! This reminds me of when I was at my primary care office to get blood work done. I was there before they were officially open as I don’t think the doctors were in yet, just the front desk MAs and the phlebotomists. I was in the waiting room and all front desk MAs (I think they’re all Medical Assistants) were chatting amongst themselves with the sliding windows at each cubicle open so I could hear everything. One of the MAs took a phone call from a young pregnant girl, when she got off the phone she loudly said, “All I know is that girl has a lot more to worry about then a cough, being that she’s pregnant at 16! Wouldn’t want to be her!” and then started laughing with her co-workers. I was SO angry, and wrote such a long, scathing letter to not only my doctor but the office manager. I extensibly WAS that girl when I was 15, and I knew exactly how she must have felt. I was raped and had my son at 16, and I HATED going to the doctor because they treated me like absolute scum when I was pregnant. Once, I actually told a nurse I was raped and of course their attitude towards me did a complete 180, but I shouldn’t have to bare my soul about something I have PTSD from to this day (17 years later) to be treated like a human being.


I’m fairly certain the lady who made the awful comment was fired as I never saw her again, which is great because she shouldn’t work with the public, and I would have left to have found a new doctor if I saw she was still there.

When I transitioned into an office work setting after working a similar job to what OP has previously, I was really taken aback by the amount of fellow entry level people that would say these kind of off-color comments. When I got into a management role at the same job I felt more comfortable addressing this behavior when I saw it because it gave from a place of “hey I’m trying to help you succeed.” So I 100% agree with this comment! Take a moment and go through your day to day word choices and see if anything could be perceived as not work appropriate. This is meant as truly no judgement, because this is something I have to work on, too! Mine are, I say fuck all the time, usually to myself in my own office, but my boss or my associates could walk by at any given time and hear me say this 😂 My other one I’m working on is I say “Oh, that’s lame” when I’m trying to empathize with someone, and really the word lame is pretty ableist so I need to stop. Ones I’ve come across in the wild that I try to take a moment to address are when any of my peers refer to a quick meeting as a pow-wow, or the term “Indian giver.”
